chunks: Ali narrated from Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot the Tawaf of the women (his wives) until he returned to his family. He said: 'He should send [someone] to perform Tawaf on his behalf. If he dies before Tawaf is performed for him, then his heir should perform Tawaf on his behalf.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', the final circumambulation of the Kaaba performed by men with their wives, completing the Hajj rituals.
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: His heir or guardian, responsible for fulfilling his religious obligations after death.
key_terms.يُطَافُ عَنْهُ: Tawaf is performed on his behalf (proxy circumambulation).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man forgets Tawaf al-Nisa' before leaving Mecca or dies before performing it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the mechanism of *Tawaf al-Nisa'* as a mandatory pillar (*rukn*) rather than a mere sunnah, establishing that its omission requires a proxy (*na'ib*) to complete the ritual. The ruling extends to posthumous completion by the heir, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the obligation remains attached to the pilgrim's estate until fulfilled, ensuring the validity of the Hajj. This underscores the importance of the final circumambulation in completing the Hajj rites according to the Ahl al-Bayt's interpretation.
